newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty seen in search for tone without foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Zloty seen in search for tone without foreigners.

text.p: The Polish zloty was unchanged against the basket of currencies in light trade and only limited bids from foreigners were expected against a strong dollar and possible central bank intervention, dealers said.

The National Bank of Poland's interventions increased the zloty volatility and players expected limited foreign investor entry at today's 800 million zloty T-bill tender which might leave the zloty searching for tone.
"Each intervention caused a nearly percentage point zloty drop (against the basket, so investment in short paper is unlikely," said a trader at a foreign company in Warsaw.

At 0930 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.17/2.10 percent from the trading band centre against opening's 2.30/2.11 percent. It was at 2.9995/05 to the dollar against opening's 2.9960/10 and at 1.8328/48 to the mark, down from 1.8300/40.
Some dealers said that the market was still uncertain about a short term intervention cap for the local unit.
"It is not clear yet whether the NBP target was not set lower," said Tomasz Wolosz from BRE SA.
The central bank depressed last week the zloty from about four percent from the central parity rate to some 2.6 percent in a series of intervention currency purchases.
One-day deposit rates were quoted unchanged at around 21 percent after the central bank refrained from draining operations on Monday.

At 0950 GMT overnight deposits were quoted at 20.90/21.15 percent against opening's 20.90/21.20 percent, tomorrow/next were at 21.00/21.25 percent against Friday's 21.10/21.25 percent. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
